lines.watchItem: Cloud spending plans were raised again this cycle and data-center chip sales set records, so orders are still running ahead of what the chain can ship. Watch whether those raised plans keep turning into firm orders across leading-edge nodes.

Advanced packaging is still the tightest link: capacity is booked through 2027 with waits of 52 to 78 weeks even as monthly output climbs toward 120,000 to 140,000 wafers. Watch whether the roughly 10 percent shortfall keeps narrowing as new lines come online.

A very small group of customers holds the packaging book: more than 85 percent is pre-booked for 2026 and 2027, with one customer near 60 percent. That leaves allocation exposed if any single one of them slows its orders.

In-house cloud silicon is growing far faster than merchant graphics parts, and NVIDIA's accelerator share keeps slipping even as its sales set records, while AMD has landed gigawatt-scale commitments it cannot ship in volume until 2027. Watch how the leading-node customer base tilts between merchant vendors and in-house designs.

End pricing stayed firm through the cycle, with TSMC reporting a 67.7 percent gross margin and full-year growth guidance lifted above 40 percent, and NVIDIA holding a 75 percent gross margin. Watch whether that firmness holds as the next wave of accelerator supply arrives.

Memory and storage scarcity is inflating rack component costs by about 2 to 3 percent a week, with memory lead times stretched to 32 to 40-plus weeks, and NVIDIA has cut memory per accelerator to stretch a fixed supply. Watch whether these part costs begin squeezing system margins and trimming order sizes.

A rival packaging route is winning real volume: Google has ordered more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for its next in-house chip, with yields reported above 90 percent at roughly half the cost. Watch whether it scales, given its own fully booked single component supplier and a weaker fit for high-bandwidth parts.

Policy and financing both sit against the demand picture: China data-center revenue fell from $9.7 billion to $4.6 billion year over year, and a growing slice of accelerator demand rests on the chip vendor's own credit support, now covering about 210,000 units. Watch whether doubts about returns on cloud spending show up as slower orders.
